Modals to express true, untrue, possible: will, may, might, could

You use the modals may, might, could and will to say if we think something is true or likely in the present.
You use them with the past participle to speculate about the possibility of something happening the past. However, will have is only for the present and future.

Look at the examples:

You may/might/could very well be right. (It's likely now)

You may/might/could have a point there. (It's not impossible)

That'll be my father on the phone. (I'm quite sure)

When speculating about the past, you use could have, would have and might have.

For example:

They may have finished already.
The nurse couldn't have had a chance to check your blood yet.

Note:
You use may not/might not to express possibility, you use could not to talk about deduction and ability.
Duncan might be planning a sequel to his last best seller.

Despite not wanting people to be considering his work as ground-breaking, he will go down in writing folklore as a gifted and unassuming genius.
He could have chosen to give up but instead he identified his strengths and persisted.
How To Write an Author Biography

An author bio is more than just information about the author. How you present the information is as important as what you are presenting. A bio is something many readers will see before ever reading a book, so its tone may lead them to make assumptions about your book's contents.

Here are some tips and ideas on how to write an author bio:

  • Title the biography with the author's name
  • Write in the third person. Example: He not I
  • Keep the length of an author biography to a maximum of 250-300 words.
What do you need to include in an author bio?

1. Where you live.
2. Work history and any writing credentials/prizes
3. Life experience and hobbies
4. Family (You need to be careful about how much information you provide)

Here are some example sentences from an author biography.
Richard Duncan is an award-winning novelist, children's author, poet and comedic writing expert.
Since then, a number of his books have received critical acclaim including, When Butterflies Cry, The Sliver, and Horace, The Hamster.
Richard's hobbies include gardening, beach walks, reading and spending time with his family.
Research your favorite author or choose one online or at a library.
Make notes based on their background.
Include information such as where they were born, their early years, successes and hobbies.
Now, write an author bio based on the information in your notes.
Be sure to organize your biography carefully. Use linking words to connect ideas.
When completed, read your biography aloud to a partner.

images.text: Richard Duncan is an award-winning novelist, children's author, poet and comedic writing expert. Originally hailing from Nantucket, an isolated island off Cape Cod, Duncan began writing in the late 80s.The spring of 2006 marked a new chapter in his life when his delightful children's book, A Mother's Gift was picked up by a local publisher. Since then, a number of his books have received critical acclaim including, When Butterflies Cry, The Sliver, and Horace, The Hamster.

Success and fame must have come as a shock to this shy,  mild-mannered writer. He might not be as extroverted as some celebrities however, his energy and enthusiasm for life drips off each page. His foray into writing might never have happened if he hadn't lost his job as a flight attendant when his first son was born. Duncan believes that his early struggles may in fact have been the key to his success. He could have chosen to give up but instead he identified his strengths and persisted.

This international best-selling author draws inspiration from the imaginations of fellow writers and credits them as much as anyone for guiding his literary journey. Richard's hobbies include gardening, beach walks, reading and spending time with his family. When he's not traveling for book signing or mentoring budding talent, you might find Richard on his sailboat with his devoted labrador retriever, off the coast of Massachusetts. You won't see him around town.  He is believed to be vacationing on the water this summer. Despite not wanting people to be considering his work as ground-breaking, he will go down in writing folklore as a gifted and unassuming genius.
